In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introgression of the PI124112 alleles at fsqs8, fsqs12, flqs8 and flqs2 loci in a ‘Piel de sapo’ background results in elongated melon fruits.

(1) the alleles at fsq2.1 are responsible for elongated melons; (2) the alleles at locus fsqs8.2 are responsible for round melons; (3) the alleles at loci fsqs8.3 and fsqs12 produce elongated fruits; and (4) the alleles at the locus fsqs8 are epistatic to fsqs2, attenuating the effects on fruit shape of the dominant A alleles at locus a.
fsqs8.0 is an allele that produces elongated melons, fsqs2.0 is an andromonoecious allele that produces elongation and fsqs8.x is the allele that produces the roundest fruits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introgression of the allele at fsqs2.2 (fsqs8.1) into ‘Pielde Sapo’ results in rounder melons.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the introgression of QTL alleles from a wild species into a cultivated variety is not straightforward, as they may interact with each other, with genes controlling other traits, or with environmental factors.
it is possible to introgress QTL for fruit shape from a very elongated melon into ‘Piel’ and produce a new variety with round melons.

the alleles at fsq8.1 are not responsible for the elongated fruit shape of the PI124112 melon, but they are responsible for the roundness of the Piel de Sapo melon, and that this effect can be overcome by introgression of the elongated allele of the fsqs8.2 locus.
